20/G.goal: Explain the VR software landscape, including virtual world generator capabilities, development tools and game engines, and native and web deployment options.
20/G.achieves: It gives the learner the foundational understanding needed to select and use VR software tools when implementing an XR system in the course case study.

20/O1.goal: Explain the functional capabilities a virtual world generator must provide for realistic and socially interactive virtual worlds.
20/O1.achieves: It lets the learner identify the physics, collision, environmental, and networked collaborative support required for believable VR experiences.

20/O2.goal: Describe how VR software development is organized, from choosing between SDKs and ready-made virtual world generators to using game engines with their development environments and core rendering, audio, and physics components.
20/O2.achieves: It lets the learner understand the major development tools and middleware services available for building VR applications and evaluate popular engines such as Unity and Unreal.

20/O3.goal: Describe how VR applications are deployed natively or over the web, distinguishing major native VR SDKs from web deployment tools and platforms.
20/O3.achieves: It lets the learner plan the platform, SDK, or web toolchain needed to deliver a VR application and assess local versus web-based delivery.
